description:
Author the predeclared, additive amendment to the pinned non-regression procedure so that its verdict attributes movement to the cutover's behaviour rather than to across-build code layout, with the tolerances and the pinned set unchanged.

## Background

The second post-cutover receipt's Falsification record establishes three bounds. Session-to-session variation of one fixed binary is small: the bit-identical control binary reproduces across two sessions at a geometric mean of 0.999314 with every cell inside ±1.9 %. Across-build variation of behaviourally identical code is large: the control arm lands outside ±5 % of the baseline at five cells, spanning 0.846 to 1.059, reproducing the effect in the same cells and directions across two sessions. And the effect reaches verdict-tripping cells: five polynomial cells move 6.6–7.8 % although no polynomial code changes between the compared revisions. Plan v1 §4's falsification record predicts that at such cells a cost-free cutover can trip the per-cell rule; the second receipt observes it doing so. Under a per-cell null that wide, the current across-build comparison cannot attribute a 5 % cell excursion to the cutover.

Owner decision DEC-E (2026-08-20) scopes the rework of the second excursion as two tracks and directs this issue as track 2: a predeclared, owner-approved, additive amendment to the verdict procedure — a same-session two-arm comparison was the direction's example — so that layout movement on untouched paths stops deciding the verdict. τ_cell stays 5 % and τ_set stays 2 %. Sibling track 1 eliminates the per-call bit-backend threshold cost; the next measured run under `50b47eae` takes both as input.

The amendment's design is this issue's decision within that direction: a same-session two-arm verdict, layout variance sampled over multiple builds per arm, a directly measured bound on the selector's cost, or another mechanism the record supports. If the chosen design needs harness support, the harness changes land with this issue; `crates/gf2-core/benches/selector_non_regression.rs` already carries the comparison modes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed predeclaration document under `dev/benchmarks/tuning_profiles/` defines, before any further measured run, the verdict comparison for the next post-cutover receipt such that across-build layout variance of behaviourally identical code is measured, bounded, or sampled inside the procedure itself, and states how a pinned cell's verdict separates cutover-attributable movement from that variance.
- [hard] REQ-02: τ_cell = 5 %, τ_set = 2 %, and the pinned thirty-four-cell set stand unchanged, and the document declares every alternative reading in advance the way `across-build-control-arm-v1.md` §2 does, so any outcome of the next run is adjudicable without a post-hoc choice.
- [hard] REQ-03: The document states which measurements constitute the baseline side of the comparison under `50b47eae` REQ-01's wording and why that wording is satisfied, and records the disposition of the 2026-08-19 baseline receipt and both failing post-cutover receipts: all stand as taken, none re-run, superseded, or adjusted.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every change to standing documents is an additive amendment: no pre-existing line of `selector-non-regression-plan-v1.md`, `across-build-control-arm-v1.md`, the baseline receipt, or either post-cutover receipt changes, and the new document cites the second receipt's Falsification record for its motivating bounds.
- [hard] REQ-05: Any harness change keeps the recorded row schema valid or bumps the schema token with the bump's consequences stated; existing comparison modes keep their behaviour, and committed tests of other issues are not edited.

## Notes

If the design concludes that no verdict procedure satisfies `50b47eae` REQ-01's wording while excluding the across-build component, the issue records that demonstration and stops for escalation; amending `50b47eae`'s criteria is the owner's decision, not this issue's.
title: Predeclare the layout-attribution amendment to the selector non-regression verdict
